title: Model Capability Shadowing: methodology and runbook for regression detection across model variants
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a repeatable 'Model Capability Shadowing' methodology that continuously compares functional behaviors (capabilities and regressions) between a canonical baseline model and incoming model variants (open forks, quantized variants, hosted replacements) used in Redwood's inference deployments. The output should be a lightweight runbook and automatable pipeline that generates actionable deltas (features lost/regressed, hallucination rate deltas, latency/cost tradeoffs) and signals to PM/Eng for rollouts or auto-fallback policies.

Why this matters: As we onboard many open and vendor models, small shifts in capability (e.g., structured output formatting, tool-calling stability, instruction-following) can materially break customer flows. Current signal sets focus on latency/cost and coarse quality metrics; we need signal fidelity tied to behavioural capabilities so product teams can make safer fallback and rollout decisions.

Success criteria (end of sprint):
- Drafted methodology doc with definitions, prioritized capability set (15 canonical checks), and test data subsets per capability.
- Working prototype pipeline that runs weekly shadow comparisons for 3 representative models and emits a ranked 'regression delta' report.
- Alert thresholds and tie-in spec for Console/Optimize to surface regressions (example dashboard widgets and webhook format).

Deliverables:
1) Shadowing methodology doc (Confluence): capability taxonomy, test harness design, thresholding heuristics, false-positive handling guidance.
2) Lightweight test datasets and prompt templates (Drive): structured output tests, instruction-following, safety/regret checks, RAG grounding micro-tests.
3) Prototype pipeline (GitHub): orchestration scripts, evaluation harness, example report generator.
4) Rollout playbook for PM/Eng: recommended actions for different delta severity levels (canary pause, auto-fallback, human review).

Approach and trade-offs:
- Start narrow: implement 15 prioritized capabilities that are high-risk for customer-facing regressions (structured output, function-calling stability, safety filters, RAG citation fidelity).
- Balance coverage vs. run cost: weekly batch runs with sampled workloads, not full production replay initially.
- Use a mix of synthetic targeted prompts and sampled anonymized customer prompts (with privacy review) to detect realistic regressions.
- Accept that some deltas are model-intent differences rather than regressions; the taxonomy and manual triage step will reduce noise.

Data sources and privacy:
- Use curated synthetic prompt sets hosted in Drive and a sampled, anonymized production prompt stream (approved by Security and Privacy).
- All sampled prompts will be stripped of PII and stored in an internal S3 workspace with limited access.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Product: Marco Ruiz (owner), Aisha Patel (PM sponsor)
- Eng: Priya Nair (inference), Leo Morales (eval infra)
- Research: Dr. Jingwei Li (eval methodology)
- DX/Console: Samantha Chen (dashboard integration)

Risks and mitigations:
- Noise/false positives: mitigate via ensemble checks and conservative thresholds; include manual triage for first 6 weeks.
- Cost of evaluation runs: start with weekly, sample-based runs and progressively increase if signal fidelity justifies it.
- Privacy/regulatory: coordinate with Security for sampled production prompt policy and data retention limits.

Acceptance criteria:
- Confluence doc reviewed and marked 'approved' by Eng and Research.
- Prototype pipeline in GitHub with CI that runs the sample suite and generates an HTML/JSON regression report.
- Two example alerts created and validated in a staging Console dashboard.

Next steps (short term):
- Week 0: finalize capability list and assemble synthetic prompt corpus.
- Week 1: spike on pipeline orchestration and minimal evaluation harness.
- Week 2: run first shadowing job across baseline and two model variants; produce first delta report.
- Week 3: iterate on thresholds and prepare dashboard spec for Console team.

Longer-term vision: integrate shadowing signals into Optimize recommendations, Dedicated rollout automation, and automatic model fallback policies to reduce customer-facing regressions during model swaps.
